q: What shape is a stop sign?
a: Eight-sided (octagon)
e: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign.
s: A stop sign is eight-sided

q: What colours is a stop sign?
a: Red background with white letters
w: White background with a red border
e: Stop = red with white letters. Yield is the one that's white with a red border.
s: has a red background with white letters

q: What shape is a yield sign?
a: A triangle
e: A yield sign is a triangle with a white background and a red border.
s: A yield sign is a triangle with a white background and a red border

q: Which sign is a triangle with a white background and a red border?
a: Yield
e: White triangle with red border = yield. The slow-moving vehicle sign is an orange triangle with a red border.
s: A yield sign is a triangle with a white background and a red border

q: A five-sided sign with a fluorescent yellow/green background warns you about…
a: A school zone
e: Five sides = school zone. Slow down and watch for children.
s: A school zone sign is five-sided and has a fluorescent yellow/green background with black symbols

q: What shape is a school zone sign?
a: Five-sided (pentagon)
e: School zone signs are five-sided, like the outline of a little school house.
s: A school zone sign is five-sided

q: What does a railway crossing sign look like?
a: X-shaped, white with a red outline
w: Round and yellow with a black X
e: The railway crossing sign is an X (crossbuck): white with a red outline.
s: A railway crossing sign is X-shaped with a white background and red outline

q: Regulatory signs (signs giving a direction you must obey) are usually…
a: Rectangular or square, with a white or black background
e: Regulatory = rectangle or square, white or black. Yellow diamond = warning. Orange = road work. Green = directions.
s: They are usually rectangular or square with a white or black background

q: Warning signs are usually…
a: Diamond-shaped, yellow with black letters or symbols
w: Triangular, orange with a red border
e: Yellow diamond = warning of something dangerous or unusual ahead.
s: They are usually diamond-shaped and have a yellow background with black letters or symbols

q: Temporary condition signs (road work, detours, lane closures) are usually…
a: Diamond-shaped, orange with black letters or symbols
e: Orange = construction, like orange cones and vests.
s: They are usually diamond-shaped with an orange background and black letters or symbols

q: Information and direction signs are usually…
a: Rectangular, green with white letters
w: Square, white with a red circle
e: Green rectangles tell you about distances and destinations.
s: They are usually rectangular with a green background and white letters

q: A sign with a green circle around a symbol means…
a: You may or must do the activity shown
w: The activity is allowed only at certain times
e: Green circle = allowed or required. Red circle with a line = not allowed.
s: A sign with a green circle means you may or must do the activity shown inside the ring

q: A red circle with a line through it on a sign means…
a: The activity shown is not allowed
w: You must do the activity shown
The activity is allowed with caution
e: Red circle + slash = NO.
s: A red circle with a line through it means the activity shown is not allowed

q: An orange triangle with a red border on the back of a vehicle means…
a: The vehicle travels at 40 km/h or less
w: You must yield to the vehicle
The vehicle is a school bus about to stop
e: That's the slow-moving vehicle sign. Slow down and stay back.
s: The “slow-moving vehicle” sign is an orange triangle with a red border

q: What does an orange diamond-shaped sign tell you?
a: There is a temporary condition, like road work or a detour
w: There is a permanent hazard, like a sharp curve
A service, like a hospital, is nearby
e: Orange = temporary condition (construction). Yellow = permanent warning.
s: These signs warn of unusual temporary conditions such as road work zones, diversions, detours, lane closures or traffic control people on the road

q: What does a yellow diamond-shaped sign tell you?
a: There is a dangerous or unusual condition ahead
w: Which way to a town or city
e: Yellow diamond = warning, such as a curve, turn, dip or sideroad.
s: These signs warn of dangerous or unusual conditions ahead such as a curve, turn, dip or sideroad

q: Which sign is the only one with eight sides?
a: Stop
e: Eight sides always means STOP.
s: A stop sign is eight-sided

q: A sign with a checkerboard border warns of…
a: Danger: a sharp turn or bend; slow down and be careful
w: The end of a construction zone
e: The checkerboard border warns of danger.
s: The checkerboard border warns of danger. Slow down; be careful.

q: Information signs are usually green. What do signs in other colours do?
a: Guide you to facilities, services and attractions
e: Other colours (like the blue wheelchair sign) point you to facilities, services and attractions.
s: Other signs with different colours guide you to facilities, services and attractions

q: Which kind of sign gives a direction that must be obeyed?
a: Regulatory
e: Regulatory signs are the rules: no left turn, one way, speed limits and so on.
s: These signs give a direction that must be obeyed

q: Besides the stop, yield, school zone and railway crossing signs, the handbook names four other kinds of signs. Which list is right?
a: Regulatory, warning, temporary conditions, and information and direction
e: Four kinds: regulatory, warning, temporary conditions, information and direction.
s: There are four other kinds of signs: regulatory, warning, temporary conditions and information and direction.

q: What shape and colour is the sign on the back of a farm tractor on the road?
a: An orange triangle with a red border
w: A white triangle with a red border
A yellow diamond with a tractor symbol
e: Farm machinery must show the orange-and-red slow-moving vehicle sign.
s: Farm machinery on the road must display an orange and red slow-moving sign on the rear of the vehicle

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Come to a complete stop
w: Slow down and go if the way is clear
Stop only if other traffic is coming
e: A stop sign always means a complete stop, even if no one is coming.
s: It means you must come to a complete stop

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Railway tracks cross the road here
e: The white X with a red outline marks a railway crossing. Slow down, look both ways, be ready to stop.
s: It warns that railway tracks cross the road

q: Which of these is a yield sign?
a: signs/3-1-3.jpg
e: The yield sign is the white triangle with the red border, pointing down.
s: A yield sign is a triangle with a white background and a red border

q: Which sign warns that you are coming to a school zone?
a: signs/3-1-2.jpg
e: The five-sided fluorescent yellow/green sign is the school zone sign.
s: It warns that you are coming to a school zone

q: Which sign marks the place where railway tracks cross the road?
a: signs/3-1-4.jpg
e: The red-and-white X (crossbuck) is at the crossing. The yellow diamond with tracks is the warning sign before it.
s: A railway crossing sign is X-shaped with a white background and red outline

q: What does this five-sided sign mean?
a: School zone: slow down and watch for children
w: School crossing: follow the crossing guard
e: Five-sided = school zone. The school crossing sign is a rectangle, and the hidden bus stop sign is a yellow diamond.
s: It warns that you are coming to a school zone. Slow down, drive with extra caution and watch for children.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Let traffic in or near the intersection go first; stop if necessary
w: The vehicle ahead goes 40 km/h or less
Come to a complete stop every time
Merge: both roads have the same right-of-way
e: Yield = let the other traffic go first. You don't have to stop if the way is clear.
s: It means you must let traffic in the intersection or close to it go first. Stop if necessary and go only when the way is clear.

q: This triangle is orange with a red border. What does it mean?
a: The vehicle ahead will travel at 40 km/h or less
w: Yield to traffic in the intersection
e: Orange triangle = slow-moving vehicle. Don't mix it up with the white yield triangle.
s: It alerts other drivers that the vehicle ahead will be travelling at 40 km/h or less

q: There's no stop line, but there is a marked crosswalk. Where must you stop for this sign?
a: At the crosswalk
w: At the edge of the intersection
Anywhere you can see both ways
e: Stop line first. No line: the crosswalk. No crosswalk: edge of the sidewalk. No sidewalk: edge of the intersection.
s: If there is no stop line, stop at the crosswalk

q: You come to this sign. What must you do?
a: Slow down, stop if necessary, and go only when the way is clear
w: Keep your speed; other drivers must yield to you
Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
e: A yield sign means let others go first. Stop only if you need to.
s: Stop if necessary and go only when the way is clear

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
a: Slow down, look both ways for trains, and be prepared to stop
w: Speed up to get across the tracks quickly
Stop only if the gates are down
e: At a railway crossing: slow down, look both ways and be ready to stop.
s: Slow down and look both ways for trains. Be prepared to stop.

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
a: Slow down, drive with extra caution and watch for children
w: Stop and wait for a crossing guard
Keep your speed; it only applies on weekends
e: School zone: slow down and watch for children.
s: Slow down, drive with extra caution and watch for children
